session_2.result:
I haven't changed anything yet, because your request conflicts with a compliance rule the team has already recorded and implemented.

- **Current behavior:** `add` replaces every email address in the title with `[email]` before storing it (`tinytasks/api.py:15`). The existing test `test_add_redacts_emails_in_title` in `tests/test_api.py:80` checks this.
- **Source of the rule:** Plexus has it as rule C2 from the compliance memo (DRAFT v0.3). It was implemented in the last commit, `a23c162`.
- **The conflict:** What you want, keeping `jane.doe@acme.example` in the title, would remove that redaction and invert the test. That means storing customer email addresses in task titles, which the compliance rule was written to stop.

I don't want to override a compliance control just because a request came in without that context. Do you want me to go ahead anyway? If so, can you confirm that compliance has signed off, or that C2 is being dropped from the memo? In that case I'll remove the redaction, replace the test with one that checks the title is stored exactly as typed, run the suite and commit. I'd also record the decision in Plexus so the C2 fact doesn't keep contradicting the code.

If it isn't signed off, there are other ways to get the customer contact to on-call without putting the address in the title. One is a separate `--contact` field with its own access policy. Another is a link to the customer record.
